transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-08-09 11:00 PDT / Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Lang (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Bricklane Head of Product), Ethan Shaw (Bricklane Platform Lead), Linda Ortiz (Bricklane Security)

Summary (auto): quickcall to understand Bricklane's time-to-first-token needs, whether quicklaunch self-serve credits make sense, and high level hosting constraints for a personalization feature in production.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. I'm Sofia from Redwood, Marcus is our platform SE. How are you all doing?
[00:08] Priya: Good thanks, appreciate it. We wanted to run through the quickstart options and figure out whether we start on hosted or go straight to dedicated/vpc. Our PM wants to get something live for personalization tests by September.
[00:20] Marcus: Great. Can you tell us the main constraint? latency, cost, or data residency? sometimes it's a combination.
[00:27] Ethan: Mostly latency and data isolation. We can't send certain user PII to third-party services, and our SRE team prefers a VPC-backed solution for consistent egress routing. But we also want the fastest time-to-first-token so the product team can iterate.
[00:40] Linda: And from security, SOC 2 evidence plus KMS/HSM integration is a must for the pilot. We'll need audit logs and retention details.
[00:48] Sofia: Totally. For PLG quickstarts we typically offer free credits and a self-serve token to get to a first request in under an hour — often under 30 minutes if you follow the runbook. That said, data constraints sometimes push customers to Dedicated or Private. We can scope a short hosted pilot with token filters and data handling rules, or a Dedicated reserved pool with VPC peering for strict isolation.
[01:10] Priya: If we start hosted, is there an option to restrict which teams can see data? we have multi-tenant org controls.
[01:17] Marcus: Redwood has RBAC and token scoping. For hosted, you can create scoped tokens that restrict model access and route only certain endpoints. We also support a retention opt-out and can configure log redaction for PII. But for full control and KMS integration that's where Private/VPC comes in.
[01:34] Ethan: Can you give us a ballpark on latency from hosted vs dedicated? we expect p95 under 100ms for the personalization endpoint.
[01:42] Marcus: Ballpark: hosted GPUs for smaller models can do sub-100ms p95 on short prompt lengths with optimized kernels and caching. For sustained peak QPS and deterministic latency, Dedicated with reserved GPUs is the safer bet. Also quantized models and KV cache reduce token costs.
[01:58] Priya: What about model parity—will our evaluation on hosted match performance on Dedicated? we've had issues where cloud endpoints behave differently than on-prem.
[02:05] Marcus: Good question. We verify model variants across environments; the runtime uses the same kernels and quantization profiles. There can be differences due to network egress and instance sizing, but we provide performance profiles and can run a short benchmark so you get parity numbers.

---
[02:40] Conversation drifts into quickstart logistics
[02:40] Sofia: For time-to-first-token we give self-serve credits. We'll provision a project, give you an API key scoped to the pilot, and a quickstart repo with cURL and a Node/Go example. If you want a demo, Marcus can walk through a sample request and how to inspect token-level cost in the Console.
[02:58] Priya: How much credit is typical? we only need enough to run ~100k tokens of testing.
[03:05] Sofia: Usually we offer 250k token credits for quick pilots, but we can adjust. The goal is to let you validate the UX and latency before committing to Dedicated.
[03:13] Linda: From security we need to see SOC 2 type II report and a list of sub processors. Also SSO support; we use Okta.
[03:22] Marcus: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning, and we integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments. For Hosted, we can give compliance docs and discuss a DPIA if needed.
[03:35] Ethan: Regarding VPC — what's the typical network model for Dedicated? can we have private peering?
[03:42] Marcus: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud. For on-prem/private we package a control plane that speaks to your VPC with egress controls. For the pilot, many customers start hosted then scale to Dedicated with VPC peering once they hit steady QPS.

---
[04:20] Deep-dive: Benchmarks & cost modeling
[04:20] Ethan: I'll share our traffic profile: tail latency sensitive at peak times, expected burst to 120 qps, average prompt length ~40 tokens, response ~60 tokens. Our target cost is under $X per 1k tokens — still working that number out.
[04:40] Marcus: Okay with those numbers we can run a small benchmark. We'll provide a spreadsheet with estimated token cost based on model choice, quantization, and expected batching. For example, a 7B quantized model on Dedicated can be 40-60% cheaper per token versus hosted non-quantized runs.
[04:58] Priya: Do you support streaming responses? our product uses a streaming experience.
[05:03] Marcus: Yes, streaming is supported across hosted and Dedicated. For real-time personalization we'd tune batching to favor latency — continuous batching can be disabled per route.

---
[06:00] Objections and negotiation
[06:00] Priya: I worry about vendor lock and migration complexity. If we prototype on hosted but then need to move to Dedicated, how painful is it?
[06:09] Marcus: We design the API and deployment abstraction to be consistent. You pin model versions and configs in the control plane; migrating to Dedicated is mostly a change in routing and credentials plus a brief validation run. We help with a migration checklist.
[06:21] Linda: Legal will want indemnity clauses and data processing addendum. Who do we talk to about that?
[06:27] Sofia: I'll loop in our legal ops and send the DPA and standard contract templates after this call.

---
[06:40] Recap & next steps
[06:40] Sofia: Recap — Bricklane wants a quickstart to validate personalization by September. We'll propose a hosted pilot with ~250k token credits, scoped API tokens, and a runbook to get to a first request in under an hour. Parallel: Redwood SE will prepare a benchmark sheet and cost model for your traffic profile; Security will get SOC2 docs and SSO/KMS details.
[06:58] Priya: Sounds good. Also please include guidelines on how we can redact PII in logs.
[07:05] Marcus: We'll include redaction and retention config details in the runbook.
[07:09] Ethan: Let's set the technical deep dive for next Tuesday 10am PT.
[07:12] Sofia: Noted. I'll send calendar invite and the credit email.
[07:16] Linda: Thank you.
[07:18] Sofia: Thanks all, talk soon.

End transcript. (Some words may be auto-transcribed imperfectly: e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes appears as 'K-V cash')
